quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Sales engineers sell business goods or services whose selling requires a technical background.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Sales Engineers) include Sales Engineer, Technical Sales Engineer, Sales Applications Engineer and Technical Marketing Engineer.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a sales engineer does
paragraphs: Sales engineers sell business goods or services whose selling requires a technical background.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Sales Engineers. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Develop, present or respond to proposals for a customer's specific requirements.
Work with sales teams to understand what the customer needs.
Visit prospective buyers to show the product.
Keep up with industry news, products, services and competitors.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
In India, the UGC specification of degrees lists B.Tech and B.E. as four-year bachelor's degrees entered after 10+2.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: B.Tech (Bachelor of Technology).
Less common routes on the map: B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering; B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering; MBA (Master of Business Administration).
